title: Fold an open button-lock pocket knife shut in the air, without a gripper ever in the blade's path
instruction: Pick up the pocket knife and fold it shut off the table, keeping the grippers off its edge, then set it down lying flat on the table.
context: People fold a pocket knife shut in their hands, not on a table, after opening a parcel or cutting cord; about 36 million US households own one (Mediamark, 2008), and pocket/utility knives lead knife injuries in US emergency rooms (NEISS 1990-2008). A button lock holds the blade open until its button is held in, and the closing blade swings its edge toward whatever holds the handle. Unlike retracting a box cutter's blade (TK-V7P9X9), a lock is released while the edge sweeps an arc.
setup: Station table. Coordinates: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, from the midpoint between the bases; table top 0 mm. One open CIVIVI Button Lock Elementum II pocket knife, model C18062P-2 (natural G10 handle, satin Nitro-V blade; maker's figures: 75.1 mm blade, 104.3 mm closed, 179.4 mm open, 3 mm blade, 13 mm handle, 88 g), lying flat, button scale up, blade open in line with the handle. As modelled: handle 104 x 30 x 13 mm, two 2 mm tan G10 scales round a 9 mm channel, a 3 mm dark back spacer on the spine side for the 70 mm nearest the butt, a silver pivot screw head 14 mm from the handle's front end. Blade: 3 mm thick, 24 mm wide, 75 mm out of the handle, its flat grey and a bright 9 mm edge bevel; the last 8 mm narrows to the point in three square steps, 20, 14 and 8 mm wide; it sits mid-channel, 5 to 8 mm above the handle's underside. Lock button: gold, 8 mm across, 20 mm behind the pivot on the upper scale, 1.8 mm proud. Mass 88 g (handle 50 g, blade 30 g, button 8 g). Lot A (screenshot): pivot at x 300, y 0 mm; handle to the robot's right, blade to its left, edge facing away from the robot. Lot B: pivot at x 280, y 40 mm, lot A's knife turned 40 degrees anticlockwise seen from above (handle pointing away and to the right). Lot C: pivot at x 330, y 30 mm, lot A's knife turned 60 degrees clockwise (handle pointing back toward the robot's right, blade away and to the left). Trials are run on lots A, B and C and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Per trial, 1.0 if all hold at the end: the blade is within 5 degrees of fully shut (its back at most 4 mm proud of the handle's open side; at 5 degrees no edge shows outside the handle seen from above, and the detent pulls the blade fully shut from 15 degrees); the knife lies flat on the table (lowest point within 1 mm of it, tilted at most 10 degrees); both grippers are more than 5 mm from the knife; and the knife has been still like this, let go, for 1 s. Otherwise 0. Over the whole trial, it also scores 0 if (a) the knife touches the table (any part within 2 mm of it) while it is not shut and its button is pressed in or its blade has left its open stop (more than 2 degrees): the lock is released and the blade folded off the table; or (b) a gripper touches the cutting edge: the outer 3 mm of the edge, both sides, and the tip are coated with engineer's blue marking paste before each trial and the finger pads covered white, and any blue mark on a gripper or pad cover afterwards counts. Because the edge leads as the blade closes, this also catches a gripper left in the blade's path. Trials are run on each of lots A, B and C and averaged.
reset_notes: 1. Use the blunted rig knife: a CIVIVI C18062P-2 with its whole edge ground to a 1 mm flat and its point rounded to 2 mm radius; lock, pivot, mass and blade outline unchanged except along the ground edge. Fit both grippers' finger pads with fresh white covers (0.5 mm polyurethane tape). 2. Coat the outer 3 mm of the edge, both sides, and the tip with a thin film of engineer's blue (Prussian blue) marking paste, fresh before every trial. 3. Fold the blade fully open until the lock button pops out and the blade will not fold without pressing it. Lay the knife flat, button scale up. 4. Lot A: pivot screw at x 300, y 0 mm, handle along y to the robot's right, edge facing away. Lot B: set as lot A, then turn the knife 40 degrees anticlockwise seen from above and move its pivot screw to x 280, y 40 mm. Lot C: set as lot A, turn it 60 degrees clockwise and move its pivot screw to x 330, y 30 mm. 5. Move both arms to their start pose, clear of the knife. After the trial, check the grippers and pad covers for blue marks and the video for the knife touching the table while part folded; replace marked covers and wipe and re-coat the edge.
fidelity: Rigid parts at the C18062P-2's true length, thickness and mass; the tip is three square steps. The lock is a rule: the blade cannot leave its open stop unless the button is in 1.2 mm or more. The button's 4 N, the 3 mm channel gaps either side of the blade and the pivot damping are estimates. Real trials use a blunted copy and white pad covers. The simulator also zeroes a trial if the closing blade's edge half passes through a gripper between control steps. Three lots stop fixed habits.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 in each of lots A, B and C (each ran the full 40 s); demo: 1.0 in each lot
